attempted_claim: Let P be a rational simply-connected polygonal domain with arctic curve A(P) having an isolated interior soft-tacnode singularity T (two smooth frozen-boundary branches with common non-lattice tangent, transverse quadratic contact, away from cusps, tangency locations and the domain boundary). For uniformly random lozenge tilings of nP viewed as non-intersecting Bernoulli paths, prove that under the tacnode scaling (order n^{2/3} tangential, n^{1/3} transverse, with explicit curvature/complex-slope constants) the local correlation functions at T converge to the continuous tacnode determinantal process of Adler-Johansson-van Moerbeke / Delvaux-Kuijlaars-Zhang, via Riemann-Hilbert steepest descent for the locally coupled non-intersecting Bernoulli-walk model with Gibbs-resampling optimal concentration at T.
decisive_failure: ['The negative assessment rests on a simplified single Bernoulli-bridge model with exact hypergeometric variance rather than a full analysis of the conditioned non-intersecting ensemble; a future sharp rigidity argument could in principle upgrade the centering, though none exists for general polygons in the available time.', 'No preset fallback existed and none was pursued; no emergent finding is claimed because the quantitative obstruction, while reproducible, does not meet the bar of an independently valuable original theorem under full Audit.', 'Literature triage used a single consolidated search call; it informed the originality assessment of the candidate increment but was not a substitute proof ingredient.']
